newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Lawmaker accuses Colombian president of murder.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker accuses Colombian president of murder.

text.p: A Colombian legislator accused President Ernesto Samper on Friday of ordering the murder of a high-profile opposition party leader in 1995.

Pablo Victoria, a member of the opposition Conservative Party in the lower chamber of Congress, said he had confidential witness statements from the case suggesting that Samper paid his personal assistant, an army colonel, 100 million pesos, or about $100,000, to kill Alvaro Gomez, a Conservative Party leader.
Colombia's chief prosecutor's office said in a terse statement that Victoria, who made the claims in an interview with Miami-based Spanish language TV channel Univision, had twisted the facts.

"The investigating authorities say they have motives to believe the claims contained in this testimony," Victoria said, in reference to a copy he obtained of a female witness' statement to the prosecutor's office.

The woman, referred to as Mrs. Cuadros Blanco in the copy of the document showed to Univision, apparently testified that Samper paid Col. German Osorio a large sum of money to kill Gomez -- a murder that sent shock-waves through the nation.
The Conservative politician and former presidential candidate was shot to death in November 1995 as he left a Bogota university where he gave law classes.

Six people, including one currently awaiting extradition from Germany, are in custody accused of the crime. Col. Osorio, Samper's former assistant, is currently under investigation for a separate murder, that of the wife of a suspected drug trafficker, in early 1996.

In a press statement issued in the wake of Victoria's comments, the chief prosecutor's office said: "The chief prosecutor emphatically rejects the unauthorised use of a confidential court statement and the interpretation made by Victoria of the statement because it does not correspond in any way to the evaluation carried out by the group of investigators."
